newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs pare losses on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs pare losses on short-covering.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures regained their poise late on Thursday as a bout of short-covering lifted the market out of its early interest rate-inspired jitters.

Both ends of the Japanese yield curve succumbed to early news reports quoting former senior Finance Ministry official Makoto Utsumi as saying Japanese bonds were overpriced and the Bank of Japan wanted to make an upward correction to the 0.5 percent official discount rate.

June Euroyen was quoted at 99.33 at 1120 GMT against its IMM close at 99.34 after hitting a low of 99.28. September recovered from a low of 99.14 to 99.19. Turnover for both months was over 28,000 contracts.
"Players decided that these were Utsumi's personal opinions and it (a rate hike) was not going to be the case. So we just went back to the opening levels," said a Japanese bank dealer.

He said the market was likely to shuffle in a range until next week, though a scheduled television appearance by Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, at around 1400 GMT could provide
Sakakibara's remarks last month that the market's view of the economy was too pessimistic pushed JGBs down across the yield curve.
"I would rather be flat just now and wait for tomorrow's opening," said the dealer.
The key March JGB contract settled at 126.33 against its previous previous 126.20. It saw a low of 125.32 earlier.
Eurodollar futures crawled to a steady finish on thin volumes ahead of Friday's non-farm payrolls report for November.
Market expectations call for a 170,000 rise in non-farm payrolls and a 5.2 percent unemployment rate.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.53 against their IMM close at 94.52. Volume was a low 4,010 contracts.
